quote: Gluten-free rice noodles are available as a substitute for the standard wheat ramen noodles (some noodle swaps carry a small fee). One reviewer specifically described ordering 'tantan ramen with soy meat and rice noodles (gluten free noodles).'

quote: The shop also notes gluten-free options on its menu and offers gluten-free cakes, indicating real awareness of gluten-free diners.

quote: Unlike most ramen shops, Towzen states it uses gluten-free soy sauce, which it boils down (along with mirin) to reduce alcohol content below 0.1%. This addresses the usual wheat-in-soy-sauce concern that makes most ramen broths unsafe for celiacs.
found: We use 100% organic soy milk in our ramen soup. We completely boil down gluten-free soy sauce and mirin to reduce the alcohol content to below 0.1%.
note: Shop's own Tabelog blurb states gluten-free soy sauce verbatim; claim is accurate.

quote: The kitchen has been fully vegan (100% plant-based) since 2018, with broth built on organic soy milk rather than meat or fish stock — so there is no cross-contact with animal products.
found: Ramen maker established since 2004 and is fully vegan since 2018. Does not use the five pungent spices.

quote: Orders are highly customizable — diners can choose flavor, spice level, portion size and noodle type, and reviewers note staff speak good English, making it easier to communicate dietary needs.

quote: The menu lists oriental-vegan, halal and gluten-free options, showing the staff routinely accommodate dietary requests.
found: Oriental vegan, halal and gluten-free options are also available.

quote: Fully vegan kitchen with no animal-product cross-contact — a rare confident choice for plant-based diners.
found: Ramen maker established since 2004 and is fully vegan since 2018. (listing category: Vegan)
note: Fully-vegan status confirmed; vegan_status 'full' is correct for this record.

All claims are true; three citations point at the wrong one of the record's own sources (reviewer quote is HappyCow not MATCHA; GF cakes are MATCHA not Tabelog; GF soy sauce is Tabelog not MATCHA). gf_confidence 'options' and vegan_status 'full' both check out (HappyCow: fully vegan since 2018; Tabelog: gluten-free soy sauce + GF options).

quote: This is a busy conveyor-belt sushi shop where many different dishes — including breaded, fried, and wheat-based items like ramen and rolls — share the same kitchen, conveyor, and shared equipment. That makes meaningful cross-contact with wheat very likely, so it should not be considered celiac-safe.
found: Gion Shijo Sta./Kaiten sushi (Conveyor belt sushi)
method: iPhone UA on s.tabelog.com; PDF via plain fetch + pdftotext
note: Tabelog only establishes the genre (conveyor-belt sushi); the wheat items and the cross-contact risk are evidenced by Sushiro's own English allergen PDF, which lists 'Iekei PorkBone Shoyu Ramen', 'Kitsune Udon Noodles', tempura items and states contact/mixing is possible - cite the PDF.

quote: Standard Japanese soy sauce (shoyu) almost always contains wheat, and the table/conveyor soy sauce at conveyor-belt sushi chains is conventional shoyu. Plain nigiri may look gluten-free, but the soy sauce typically is not — bring your own certified gluten-free tamari if you are celiac.
found: Most, but not all, Japanese soy sauces include wheat as a primary ingredient... Tamari: It contains little or no wheat. Wheat-free tamari can be used by people with gluten intolerance.
method: plain fetch of both Wikipedia articles
note: The cited Sushiro article never mentions wheat, gluten or soy-sauce composition (its only 'soy sauce' hits are the 2023 bottle-licking prank); the wheat-in-shoyu fact is on the Soy sauce article. Nothing anywhere evidences what soy sauce sits on Sushiro's tables - drop or soften that sub-clause.

quote: A handful of items (such as inari, cucumber rolls, certain sides and desserts) may appear plant-based, but everything rides a shared conveyor and is prepared in a fish- and seafood-heavy kitchen, so cross-contact with fish, shellfish, and egg is expected. Sauces and broths frequently use dashi (fish stock). Confirm ingredients item by item.
found: *Since manufacturing plants and stores also handle ingredients containing other allergens that are not originally contained in the product, there is a possibility that these substances may come into contact with or get mixed into the product.
method: plain fetch of the EN site; allergen PDF linked from it, read with pdftotext
note: The English homepage lists menu items (Cucumber, Corn, Kitsune Udon) but says nothing about cross-contact or dashi; the contact/mixing statement is in the linked allergen PDF. Also note the homepage shows no 'inari' item, so that example is unsourced.

quote: Sushiro publishes chain-wide allergen information for its menu items, which can help identify which dishes contain major allergens; however, no location-specific allergy-handling practices for the Gion branch were found, so confirm directly with staff before ordering.
found: Allergen information (links to www3.akindo-sushiro.co.jp/pdf/menu/allergy_en.pdf) / Allergen Information (Dotonbori Store)
note: Chain-wide EN allergen chart is published and linked from the cited page; it is indeed store-generic apart from one Dotonbori-specific chart, so the Gion caveat is accurate.

quote: The menu and ordering are touch-panel based with published chain-wide allergen charts, so you can look up listed allergens for individual items before ordering.
found: Multilingual touch panel - You can order your favorite products from a touch panel that supports multiple languages: English, Chinese (simplified), and Korean.
note: Both halves (touch panel, allergen chart) are on the cited page.

quote: As a slightly off-center Gion location, it can be calmer than the busiest downtown shops, which may make it easier to take time and ask questions about ingredients.
found: The Gion branch is located in a tourist area... / I visited Sushiro, which had a long line of overseas guests during the New Year holidays.
note: The cited page points the other way - reviewers call it a tourist area with long queues. Delete this 'positive'; it is invented atmosphere, and it is the sentence that tells a celiac they will have time to ask questions.

One claim ('calmer than the busiest downtown shops') is unsupported and contradicted by the cited page; three others cite pages that do not carry their substance. gf_confidence 'options' is generous for a shop the record itself says is not celiac-safe - there is no GF soy sauce and the allergen PDF flags shared-line contact; vegan_status 'options' is fine.

quote: Falafel is deep-fried, and the menu also serves wheat-based pita and fried sides (fries) in the same kitchen. No source describes a separate fryer or dedicated gluten-free prep area, so cross-contamination in the oil and on shared surfaces should be assumed possible...
found: Falafel is a deep-fried ball made from ground chickpeas. / 5 variations of pitasand (Arabian style sandwich)
note: Deep-frying and wheat pita are on the cited page and it says nothing about a separate fryer; the 'fries' detail is only on the Tabelog menu tab (French fries, Fried Spicy Pita) - harmless but not on this page.

quote: This is Middle Eastern / Israeli cooking (falafel, hummus, kebab, tahini-based sauces) rather than Japanese cuisine, so wheat-containing Japanese soy sauce is not a typical ingredient...
found: Israeli food Take-out, delivery, online-shop vegan-multiethnic food / the Israeli owner says...

found: There's a picture menu and the owner speaks fluent English.

found: Hummus Paste / Baba Ganoush / Green Salad / 'Pita Sandwich' packed with fresh vegetables, perfect for vegans!
method: iPhone UA on s.tabelog.com incl. the listing's /dtlmenu/ tab
note: Dish list confirmed on the same Tabelog listing's menu tab; the 'naturally gluten-free by recipe' framing is recipe reasoning, not a page statement, but it is not contradicted.

CITATIONS mostly hold, but the RECORD's vegan_status is wrong: 'full' on a restaurant whose own cited page says it serves 'meals made with a variety of ingredients such as chicken', whose Tabelog menu lists chicken kebab, 'Veggie Salad with Cheese and Olives' and cheesecake, and whose own site advertises chicken-kebab pita. Must be downgraded to 'options'. gf_confidence 'options' is fine (japanese-heart tags Wheat free / グルテンフリー).

found: HappyCow reviews: 'the two vegan lunch sets - a "fried soy chicken" and teriyaki wheat gluten' / 'We ate the fried gluten chicken with choice of 3 fresh salads, brown rice and miso soup'

note: TWO RECORD-LEVEL PROBLEMS, both safety-relevant. vegan_status 'full' IS WRONG and the record's own text says so - Tabelog's menu lists Meat Hummus (spicy minced meat), Passionate Shawarma (grilled chicken), egg-based Sabich and shakshuka with a sausage topping, and Tabelog tags it 'Vegan options'. Downgrade to 'options'. Two more claims cite the shop homepage for menu facts that only exist on Tabelog (the site's menus are image PDFs). gf_confidence 'options' is consistent with Tabelog's 'Gluten-Free options' tag.
